newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice prices stable as Tet holiday begins.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice prices stable as Tet holiday begins.

text.p: Vietnam's export rice market was quiet on Wednesday as the country began marking the Tet Lunar New Year holiday.

Few dealers were working after midday local time in Ho Chi Minh City. Those who were said five percent broken grade had been trading unchanged from a week ago at around $270-$275 per tonne FOB Saigon Port.
"It's been very quiet. There's only one ship loading in Saigon Port and everyone's in a holiday mood," said a regional trader.
He said the ship was bound for Malaysia but gave no details of the quantity of rice involved.
Rumours last week of a possible deal between Manila and Hanoi for the purchase of up to 200,000-300,000 tonnes of local rice appeared to have evaporated.

The government said earlier this week it expected to export at least 2.6 million tonnes of rice this year and possibly more, despite recent prolonged flooding in the main producing area, the Mekong Delta.
In 1996 Vietnam sold some 3.1 million tonnes of rice to overseas buyers making it the world's third largest rice exporter, after Thailand and the United States.
